title: Cholera pandemics of the 1800s
summary: In the nineteenth century cholera spread from India across the world. The first pandemic began in 1817 at Jessore near Calcutta and reached the Far East, Muscat, Tehran and Baghdad; a second, from 1829, crossed into Russia, Europe and America. Three more followed by 1896, mostly starting in India and carried by trade and by pilgrims to Mecca, and a sixth began in 1899. These pandemics killed millions, and in 1849 John Snow linked a London outbreak to sewage-tainted drinking water.

uncertainty.note: Five pandemics fall within 1817-1896; a sixth ran from 1899 to 1923 (Azizi and Azizi 2010).

as_recorded.value: The first pandemic (1817 - 1821) known as ‘Asiatic cholera’ began in Jessore near Calcutta
The first pandemic, or global epidemic, was recorded in the 19th century. Since then, six pandemics have killed millions of people worldwide.
The fifth pandemic (1881-1896) began in India and reached Europe

where.historical_name: Jessore, Bengal Presidency, British East India Company

importance.justification: Repeated pandemics across Asia, Europe and the Americas killed millions and drove the study of water-borne disease (R4 D2 T2 L3).

audience_note: Describes mass deaths from epidemic disease.

related.because: The 1854 Broad Street outbreak in London was a localized epidemic within the third nineteenth-century cholera pandemic.
